transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you. Um, well, I guess I'm here because... my husband sort of pushed me to come. He and the people at the warehouse, they keep acting like I'm... well, like I'm crazy. Which I'm really not, I promise. I try to be a good worker. 

It's just that I know they've been watching my moves on the floor, and... and they keep changing my pallet counts. I'm pretty sure they're just doing it to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. That's a normal thing to be frustrated about, right? I hope I'm explaining that okay.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people around you cannot hear?

Um... well, I guess... I mean, I don't want you to think I'm, like, really losing it or anything. It's probably just the warehouse echoing, you know? But sometimes, when I'm pulling stock in the aisle, or even just at home folding laundry... I hear this man's voice. It's really clear, like he's standing right next to me, and he just says, "Nicole, check it again." But then I look, and nobody's there. That's just stress playing tricks on me, right? A lot of people get that when they're working hard, don't they?
Have you noticed any periods where your mood felt extremely high, or perhaps very low, for a week or more at a time?

Um... well, I don't know if I'd call it extremely high. I really don't want to sound like I'm out of control or anything. But... I do have days, sometimes a whole week of them, where I just feel really... fired up? Like nobody can slow me down. I get so much done, which is a good thing, right? Everybody wants to be productive. 

But, um... I guess the hard part is... well, I hate admitting this because I really try to be a good wife. But when I'm feeling that way, if my husband asks me just one small question about the kids or what my schedule is, I kind of... I snap at him. I don't mean to, it just suddenly feels like he's trying to control me when I'm finally doing great. I always feel awful about it later. It's normal to get a little short-tempered when you're just trying to keep everything on track, isn't it?
When you hear that man's voice, does it only happen during those times when you are feeling 'fired up' and energetic, or does it also happen when your mood is feeling more normal or low?

Um... well... I guess I've heard it at other times, too. I mean, I try to keep track, but I don't want you to think it's, like, an everyday, all-the-time thing. It's really not that bad. 

But, um... yeah, even a few weeks ago, when things were quieter... I was actually sleeping pretty good, getting my normal hours, and I wasn't feeling all rushed or racing around or anything. I was just having a regular week. But... I still heard him. Just that same voice, telling me to check things. And... and I still knew they were messing with my pallet counts at work, even though I was feeling fine. 

That just means I'm paying close attention to my job, right? It doesn't mean I'm... you know, really sick or anything, does it?

Looking back over the last six months or so, have there been any periods lasting at least two weeks where you experienced those voices or the feeling that people were watching you, even when you were not feeling particularly high or low in your mood?

Um... yeah, I guess so. I mean, like I was saying before, it's not like it's taking over my life or anything. I really don't want you to worry too much about it. 

But, um... yeah, looking back, there was that time a little while ago... maybe a few weeks or so? I was feeling totally normal. Like, I was getting a solid eight hours of sleep, my mood was just... regular. I wasn't snapping at my husband or running around trying to do a million things at once. But... I still heard the man's voice. He was still telling me to check my work. And... and I was still so sure that people at the warehouse were purposely messing with my pallet counts to get me in trouble. 

But I mean, two weeks isn't that long, right? It's just a little blip. That doesn't mean it's anything too serious, does it?

Looking back over the past year, have you experienced those voices or the feeling that people were watching you for a total of six months or more, even if those feelings went away for a little while in between?

Um... well, it hasn't been a whole year, I don't think. I really try to just focus on my work and my family, you know? I don't want to make a big deal out of it. 

But... I guess if I really think about it... the voice, and feeling like the guys at the warehouse are messing with my stuff... it's probably been going on for, um, maybe about eight months? Give or take? But it's not like I'm crazy or anything, right? Eight months sounds like a long time, but I still go to work every day and do my job. That shows I'm handling it okay, doesn't it?

Looking back over those eight months, would you say that the times you felt 'fired up' or very low happened most of the time, or were they just occasional short periods compared to the times your mood felt more normal?

Um... well... I guess if I really look at the whole eight months... it's mostly been the fired-up times. I mean, I really don't want it to sound like I'm out of control or anything, because I'm not! I'm still getting things done. 

But, um... yeah, for more than half of that time, I've been in that mode where I just don't need much sleep at all, and I take on a lot of extra tasks at the warehouse. And... well, I guess I do get a little snappy with my husband or the guys at work if they try to tell me to slow down or take a break. But that's just because I'm a hard worker, right? It's good to be productive and want to get things done quickly, isn't it? I just... I hope you don't think I'm a bad person for getting a little irritable sometimes.
